main_text.p: tradidit eam Josepho filio Justitiæ, filio Josephi sacerdotis in Damasco, & correxit eam Abraham de filiis Matar anno nongentesimo & vicesimo regni Ismaelitarum decima mensis Elul, itaqve anno Christi, 1542. scriptus est, character & papyrus alteram ætatem non videntur arguere; dicam præterea sectiones istius codicis sectionibus nostri omnino pares esse, unoqve & eodem nomine קציץ appellari in fine Geneseos 250. adnotantur; in fine Exodi 200, in fine Levit. 130. totidem in nostro iisdem locis numerantur, ad finem Numerorum & Deuter. in tuo omissæ sunt: sed æqvalitatem ubiqve esse non ambigo.

Petis à me expressionem istorum verborum, in nomine Patris & Filii & Spiritus sancti, Hebraice & Samaritice; sic Hebraice efferri debent beschem abuben veruach haqvodesch, בשם אב ובן ורוח הקדש Samaritani ita efferent[?]: [illegible, ~8 letters] qvomodo pronuntient ista Samaritani, hoc est, ut Judæorum more loqvar, qvibus punctis loqvendo

page.notes: Samaritan-script words after "efferent:" are not legible on the scan; marked illegible. An ink blot covers the letter(s) between "fer" and "t" in "efferent"; read as "ferent" with [?]. The Hebrew words "בשם" and "אב ובן ורוח הקדש" are copied as printed. The line "more loqvar, qvibus punctis loqvendo" appears in heavier type on the scan; no italic is recorded for it. The Hebrew term "קציץ" is copied from the scan and is in the printed text. Old-style figures (1542, 250, 200, 130) are copied as printed. The catchword "illa" is the first word of the next page.
